patch_resolves_note: On the original PoC, the fixed build still reaches the `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN` branch in `fasthuf_initialize()` but stops at the inserted `currByte >= topByte` truncation guard when `currByte` reaches `topByte`, so the extra 8-bit read is skipped and the heap-buffer-overflow disappears. On the adjacent one-byte boundary mutation that increases the admitted Huffman payload by exactly one byte, the same fixed guard is exercised genuinely with `currByte < topByte`, the protected read executes, and the run remains clean.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant attacker data on the reproduced path. The PIZ decoder reads the next 32-bit field from the packed chunk as the byte length of the Huffman-coded payload that will be handed to `internal_huf_decompress()`.
Root cause. After a `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN` marker has been read, vulnerable code requests the extra 8-bit run length without first checking whether `currByte` has already reached `topByte`.

ASan sink. `fasthuf_read_bits()` refills its bit buffer by dereferencing `*currByte` even though `currByte` has already reached `topByte`, so the byte load lands exactly one byte past the packed chunk buffer.

nodes.state: At the `while (*bufferNumBits < numBits)` refill loop, the vulnerable sink execution enters the loop because the buffered-bit count is still below the requested 8-bit extra run-length read.
